Marketing audiences

Sources collect choices. Franchise rules interpret them. SFMC selects the final audience.

How it works

These three policies are fictional examples, not franchise-specific operating rules.

Collect → interpret → activate

Wi-FiSource owner

Captures a person and the permission wording presented at collection.

Instagram / formsMarketing operations

Keeps the original submission, brand, purpose and opt-in choice.

identities + choices
Warehouse consentData engineering

Preserves evidence and applies the approved franchise policy. An absent choice is not an opt-in.

eligible feed
SFMC audienceMarketing / SFMC owner

Imports the feed, then applies segment, suppression, journey and send rules. Warehouse eligibility is not the final send list.

Franchise policy branches

HarborExplicit permission

Illustrative policy: require a recorded opt-in for this purpose; later opt-out suppresses.

SummitRetain known choice

Illustrative policy: a new source with no choice preserves a known choice; later opt-out suppresses.

ValleyReview unknown choice

Illustrative policy: keep unknown choices out until reviewed; later opt-out suppresses.

The return path

SFMC opt-outSFMC owner

Records the withdrawal and applies destination suppression.

consent event
Warehouse historyData engineering

Stores the return event and applies the correct franchise rule before the next eligible feed.

Engineering owns the agreed feed and consent transformation. Marketing owns the collection language, policy decisions, and final SFMC selection.

Try one example

The warehouse expects 1,200 members. The next transfer contains 35 new members. The campaign destination starts with 1,177 members, including 14 retained from an older audience.

Rules and supporting detail

The complete loop

Source records
→
Audience rules
→
Campaign destination
→
Response events
↩
Return to the next audience

Response events → stored consent changes → audience rules → next campaign selection

Audience rules select eligible people. A transfer updates the campaign destination. A separate comparison reconciles membership. Opens, clicks, and withdrawals return through an event feed; the next audience changes only after the relevant rule consumes them.

Consent and audience membership answer different questions. A person may belong to a segment and still be ineligible for a particular message.

What the counts can prove

ObservationWhat it establishesStill needed
35 rows transferredThe transferred rows were processedFull membership comparison
Both sides show 1,200The counts agreeCompare the same member IDs
Withdrawal event receivedThe event reached storageApply consent before the next selection
How the example handles privacy

All counts and records are synthetic. The controls update an in-memory model and send no campaign, export, or personal information.
